water.d: The universal solvent of life; a bent polar molecule whose hydrogen bonds shape its properties.

h2.d: H2; the lightest molecule, a clean-burning fuel and the most abundant element in the universe.

o2.d: O2; a diradical diatomic gas that makes up 21 percent of air and powers respiration.

n2.d: N2; held together by a strong triple bond, it makes up 78 percent of air.

co2.d: Linear O=C=O; product of respiration and combustion and the main long-lived greenhouse gas.

nh3.d: Pungent trigonal pyramidal gas made by the Haber process; the basis of nitrogen fertilizers.

hcl.d: Acrid gas that dissolves in water to give hydrochloric acid, the acid in stomach juice.

hbr.d: Corrosive gas that forms hydrobromic acid in water; a reagent for making alkyl bromides.

naoh.d: Lye; a strong base found in drain and oven cleaners and used in traditional soap making.

nacl.d: Table salt; the ionic crystal that seasons food and makes seawater salty.

br2.d: Br2; one of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature, red-brown and fuming.

cl2.d: Cl2; a yellow-green toxic gas used to disinfect water and to make PVC.

hno3.d: Planar HNO3 with a resonance-delocalized nitro group; a strong oxidizing acid.

so2.d: Bent gas from burning sulfur-containing fuel and volcanoes; a cause of acid rain.

boh3.d: Trigonal planar B(OH)3, a weak Lewis acid that forms layered hydrogen-bonded sheets.

methane.d: Simplest alkane and main component of natural gas; a potent greenhouse gas.

ethane.d: Two-carbon alkane from natural gas, mainly cracked to make ethylene.

methanol.d: Simplest alcohol; a toxic solvent, fuel and feedstock, and the antifreeze in washer fluid.

ethanol.d: Drinking alcohol and a common lab and fuel solvent, made by yeast fermentation of sugars.

propan2ol.d: Rubbing alcohol; a disinfectant and cleaning solvent for electronics and skin.

aceticacid.d: The acid that gives vinegar its sour taste and sharp smell; also a major industrial chemical.

ethylene.d: Simplest alkene and monomer of polyethylene, the most produced plastic; also a plant hormone.

propene.d: Three-carbon alkene polymerized into polypropylene for packaging, fibers and car parts.

butadiene.d: Conjugated diene monomer of polybutadiene and SBR synthetic rubber used in tires.

cyclohexene.d: A cyclic alkene with one C=C double bond; a standard substrate for addition reactions.
cyclohexene.a: C C C C C C

benzene.d: Prototype aromatic ring: six carbons with six delocalized pi electrons and equal bond lengths.
benzene.a: C C C C C C

toluene.d: Methylbenzene; a common solvent in paints, adhesives and lab work, and an octane booster.
toluene.a: C C C C C C C

phenol.d: A hydroxyl group on a benzene ring; more acidic than alcohols and a resin feedstock.
phenol.a: O C C C C C C

formaldehyde.d: Simplest aldehyde; a gas used with phenol, urea or melamine to make thermoset resins and in POM.

acetaldehyde.d: Two-carbon aldehyde made when the body oxidizes ethanol; a cause of hangover symptoms.

acetone.d: Simplest ketone; the fast-evaporating solvent in nail polish remover and lab glass rinses.

benzaldehyde.d: Simplest aromatic aldehyde, with the odor of bitter almonds and cherries.
benzaldehyde.a: O C C C C C C C

ch3cl.d: Methyl chloride; produced naturally by oceans and plants, and a silicone feedstock.

ch3br.d: Methyl bromide; a former soil fumigant phased out because it depletes ozone.

bromobenzene.d: An aryl halide, Ar-Br; used to make phenyl Grignard reagents and in cross-coupling.
bromobenzene.a: Br C C C C C C

ac2o.d: A carboxylic anhydride, R-CO-O-CO-R; used to make cellulose acetate and aspirin.
ac2o.a: O O O C C C C

acetylcl.d: An acyl chloride, R-CO-Cl; a reactive acylating agent that fumes in moist air.

phboh2.d: A boronic acid, R-B(OH)2; a partner in Suzuki cross-coupling reactions.

glucose.d: Six-membered ring form of glucose with an axial anomeric OH; the unit of starch and glycogen.
glucose.a: O O O O O O C C C C C C

ethylacetate.d: Sweet-smelling ester solvent in nail polish remover and chromatography; also decaffeinates coffee.

aspirin.d: Acetylsalicylic acid, an NSAID for pain, fever and clot prevention; marketed by Bayer in 1899.
